title: Audience Velocity Briefing — Engineering Trio
content:
Purpose:
This briefing is a compact, action-first guide for GTM, SDRs, and SEs to rapidly connect Redwood Inference’s differentiated value to three tightly related engineering audiences: ML Engineers, Backend Engineers, and Platform Teams. The focus is on velocity-oriented messaging — how to get a prospect from discovery to a pilot with measurable SLOs within 4–8 weeks.

Executive TL;DR (one paragraph):
ML engineers care about fidelity, debugging, and model lifecycle ergonomics. Backend engineers care about predictable latency, throughput, and integration simplicity. Platform teams care about governance, capacity planning, and cost predictability. Redwood wins when we lead conversations with measurable SLOs (p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens), concrete escape hatches (dedicated capacity, private deployment), and a demo that shows identical API behavior across hosted/dedicated/private in <15 minutes.

How to use this doc:
- SDR: use the 15s hooks and one-liners for outreach.
- AE/SE: expand into the 5–15 minute discovery and demo scripts, focusing on the persona priorities.
- Solutions: use the objection handlers and rollout patterns for proposals and SOWs.

Persona briefs (core needs + trigger signals):
1) ML Engineer (persona shorthand: "MLE")
- Core needs: reproducible quality, rapid iteration on prompts and model variants, easy evaluation and regression detection.
- Trigger signals: evaluation failures, sudden quality regressions after model updates, need to serve multi-model experiments.
- Primary KPIs: evaluation pass rate on test prompts, time-to-iterate on model + prompt (hrs), relative quality vs baseline.
- Velocity hook (15s): "Run AB tests across model variants with identical API calls and automatic regression alerts — get quality-safe rollouts in days, not months."

2) Backend Engineer (persona shorthand: "BE")
- Core needs: deterministic latency under load, predictable tail latency, simple SDKs and retry semantics, observability per route.
- Trigger signals: customer-facing latency spikes, inability to meet SLOs with current endpoints, bursty traffic patterns.
- Primary KPIs: p50/p95 latency, 99th percentile SLA, error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
- Velocity hook (15s): "Move from experiment to production with out-of-the-box SLOs, per-route latency dashboards, and automatic graceful fallbacks if capacity is constrained."

3) Platform Team (persona shorthand: "Platform")
- Core needs: predictable spend, capacity isolation for critical workloads, security and auditability, rollout controls across orgs.
- Trigger signals: requests for dedicated capacity, procurement reviews, auditors asking about data residency/KMS, rising cloud spend.
- Primary KPIs: cost variance vs budget, utilization of reserved pools, time to provision capacity, compliance evidence lag.
- Velocity hook (15s): "Deliver predictable performance across teams via reserved pools, versioned deployments, and audit trails — reduce unpredictable cloud spend and mean time-to-provision to days."

Differentiated value props (ordered by cross-persona resonance):
- Unified API surface: same SDK calls and schema across hosted/dedicated/private — fewer integration branches.
- Production-grade runtime: latency-optimized serving with continuous batching and KV cache management.
- Cost-performance controls: autoscaling + work-aware batching + quantization guidance that map to clear cost delta estimates.
- Safe rollouts + observability: route-level dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and regression alerts tied to eval suites.
- Enterprise controls: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs.

Competitive framing & short rebuttals (soundbites for field use):
- Against cloud-managed endpoints (AWS/GCP): "They give infra primitives; we give an inference runtime + orchestration designed for LLM patterns (KV cache, attention optimizations, model variants) and product tooling that maps directly to ML/SE KPIs."
- Against LLM API pure-play vendors: "APIs are simple — but they rarely offer predictable capacity and private deployment options. We bridge developer velocity with enterprise-grade capacity controls."
- Against self-hosted runtime vendors: "Self-hosted provides control but large ops cost. Redwood accelerates time-to-production with a runtime tuned for fairness across throughput/latency/cost and offers private installs when ops bandwidth exists."

Demo/Discovery scripts (15m discovery | 15m demo):
- Discovery (15m):
  - Intro + one-liner (60s).
  - Quick context: what workload? (LLM type, prompt shapes, QPS, latency expectations) (5m).
  - Pain probes: quality regressions, SLO misses, procurement/compliance blockers (5m).
  - Commit to pilot success criteria (p50/p95 latency target, cost target, dataset for eval) (4m).
- Demo (15m):
  - Live: show identical API call against hosted and dedicated model variant (3m).
  - Show route-level latency/cost dashboard and token-level breakdown for a representative flow (4m).
  - Show rollout: pin a model version, rollout 10% canary, automatic fallback policy (4m).
  - Show private deployment checklist (networking, KMS, audit logs) and quote turn-around for pilot (4m).

Objection handlers (short templates):
- "We can't risk quality regression if we change runtime": "We tie rollouts to eval suites and regression alerts; you can require passing thresholds before promotion."
- "We already have cost controls in our cloud": "We show cost deltas across model/quantization combos and give reserved pools to stabilize unit economics. Many teams find their monthly variability drops 20–40%."
- "We need on-prem for compliance": "Private deployment is a supported path — you keep the control plane and we help with packaging and hardening for audits."

Playbook for pilot success (4–8 week timeline):
- Week 0: kickoff, success criteria, and access. Provide a lightweight integration checklist.
- Week 1: ingest evaluation prompts + baseline run. Deploy a safe canary on hosted.
- Week 2–3: measure latency/cost at target QPS, tune batching/quantization settings.
- Week 4: demonstrate deterministic rollout to dedicated/private; finalize capacity sizing.
- Week 5–8: optional pilot extension for heavy load test, compliance handoff, and SOW for reserved capacity.

Suggested demo artifacts to attach to emails:
- 1-page SLO target template (pre-filled with common targets).
- Short script for evaluating 50 golden prompts and the dashboard output.
- Comparison table: hosted vs dedicated vs private (latency, cost, ownership, time-to-provision).

Persona-specific win conditions (what success looks like to them):
- MLE: automated regression alerts triggered by evals, reduced time-to-iterate on prompts, reproducible A/B across model variants.
- BE: sustained p95 under target at expected QPS, clear per-route tracing for token billing, fewer outages related to model capacity.
- Platform: reserved pool utilization >80% with predictable monthly spend; documented audit trail for model access and KMS usage.

Metrics & evidence to collect during pilot (what the AE must record):
- p50/p95/p99 latency at baseline and after tuning.
- Token cost per 1k tokens across model/quantization settings.
- Eval regression rate and number of blocked promotions avoided.
- Time from request to provision dedicated capacity (days).

Field scripts — short language for outreach (15s / 60s / email subject lines):
- 15s SDR: "We help teams keep LLM models in production with stable latency and measurable cost controls — can I send a 1-page SLO template?"
- 60s AE: "We can run 50 representative prompts and show where quality or latency will change across model variants and deployment modes — if you’re hitting SLO or cost surprises, we can quantify a fix in two weeks."
- Email subject lines: "Quick: SLO template for LLM latency and cost", "Showcase: 50 prompt eval + latency baseline for your flow"

Open questions (for product/engineering to clarify for field):
- Default quantization profiles: map from workload archetypes to recommended profiles and expected % cost delta (need a concise one-pager).
- Standard turnaround times for private deployments (pre-flight checklist + typical lead times by region).
- Benchmarks for token-level billing discrepancies and how to present them to finance.

Next steps / asks from GTM/Product/Ops:
- Product: produce a 1-page quantization delta cheat sheet for field.
- Solutions: a short template SOW for 30/60/90 day pilots including reserved pool SKU options.
- Marketing: create a short demo video (2–3 minutes) showing identical API behavior across hosted/dedicated/private.

Appendix — quick reference lines per persona: (one-liners for rapid copy-paste)
- MLE: "Versioned model rollouts + eval-tied gates = fast, safe iteration on prompts and weights."
- BE: "Observable, route-level latency and token cost with graceful fallback keeps user-facing SLAs steady under peaks."
- Platform: "Reserved pools and per-route cost insights let you forecast spend and avoid surprise bills."

Document provenance: authored by Leah Kim (GTM), reviewed by Jonah Reyes (SE) and Priya Desai (Product).
